translations.idiomatic: The emperor stopped play, could not walk, and took to his bed with vertigo.

sentences.zh: 自是外不聞上起居者三日。

translations.literal: From then for three days the outer court heard nothing of the Emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: For three days the court heard nothing of the emperor's condition.

sentences.zh: 是夜，月近房。

translations.literal: That night, the moon drew near the Room mansion.
translations.idiomatic: That night the moon neared the Room mansion.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁亥朔，詔五坊鷹隼並解放，獵具皆毀之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, dinghai new moon — an edict released all Five Wards hawks and falcons; hunting gear was all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth month opened with freeing the palace hawks.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，宰臣李逢吉率百僚至延英門請見，上不許。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Chief Minister Li Fengji led the hundred officials to Yanying Gate requesting audience — the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Li Fengji was turned away at Yanying Gate.

sentences.zh: 中外與度等三上疏，請立皇太子。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court, together with Pei Du and others, thrice submitted memorials requesting establishment of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Court and ministers thrice begged for a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 是夜，司徒、中書令韓弘卒。

translations.literal: That night, Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery Han Hong died.
translations.idiomatic: That night Han Hong died.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上於紫宸殿禦大繩床見百官，李逢吉奏景王成長，請立為皇太子，左僕射裴度又極言之。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the Emperor at Zichen Hall mounted the great rope bed and received the hundred officials; Li Fengji memorialized that Prince Jing had come of age and requested he be made crown prince; Left Vice Director Pei Du also spoke forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the ailing emperor received officials and heard pleas for Prince Jing.

sentences.zh: 癸已，詔景王為皇太子。

translations.literal: On guisi, an edict made Prince Jing crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Prince Jing was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 淮南奏和州饑，烏江百姓殺縣令以取官米。

translations.literal: Huainan memorialized Hezhou famine; Wujiang commoners killed the magistrate to seize official grain.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan reported famine and a magistrate killed for grain.

sentences.zh: 甲午，內出絹二百匹，賑兩市癃殘窮者。

translations.literal: On jiawu, two hundred bolts of silk were issued from the inner palace to relieve the crippled poor of the two markets.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu silk relieved the capital's destitute.

sentences.zh: 己未，兩軍容內司公主戚屬之家，並以上疾痊平，諸寺為僧齋。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the two armies' commissioners, inner offices, princesses, and affinal kin — all because the Emperor's illness had fully recovered — held vegetarian feasts at various temples.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the court celebrated the emperor's recovery with temple feasts.

sentences.zh: 仍敕在京諸司疏放系囚。

translations.literal: Still an edict ordered capital offices to review and release prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were ordered released.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上御宣政殿冊皇太子。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Emperor attended Xuanzheng Hall to invest the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the crown prince was invested.

sentences.zh: 受冊畢，百僚謁太子于東宮，太子舉簾，執笏答拜，宮僚拜則受之。

translations.literal: When investiture was complete, the hundred officials visited the crown prince at the Eastern Palace; the crown prince raised the curtain, held the tablet, and returned bows; when palace officers bowed he received them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then paid court to the new heir with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 丁未，判度支、戶部侍郎張平叔貶通州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingwei, revenue judge and Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Pingshu was demoted to Tongzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Zhang Pingshu was exiled to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 是夜，月掩左角。

translations.literal: That night, the moon occulted the Left Horn.
translations.idiomatic: That night the moon eclipsed the Left Horn.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以前天平軍節度使馬總檢校左僕射、守戶部尚書。

translations.literal: On jiyou, former Tianping military commissioner Ma Zong was made acting Left Vice Director, acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Ma Zong was named acting left vice director.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以吏部侍郎竇易直為戶部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Vice Minister of Personnel Dou Yizhi was made Vice Minister of Revenue and revenue judge.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Dou Yizhi took revenue.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以太子冊禮畢，宣制赦囚徒。

translations.literal: On guichou, because crown prince investiture rites were complete, an edict proclaimed amnesty for prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou investiture amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 以前黔中觀察使崔元略為鄂、嶽、蘄、黃、安等州觀察使。

translations.literal: Former Qianzhong observation commissioner Cui Yuanlue was made E-Yue-Qi-Huang-An observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanlue took the E-Yue command.

sentences.zh: 太子賓客孟簡卒。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Guest Meng Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jian died.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以前陝虢觀察使衛中行為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: On yimao, former Shan-Guo observation commissioner Wei Zhongxing was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Wei Zhongxing became right vice director.

sentences.zh: 是冬十月頻雪，其後恆燠，水不冰凍，草木萌發，如正二月之後。

translations.literal: That winter in the tenth month snow fell repeatedly; afterward it was constantly warm, water did not freeze, grass and trees sprouted — as after the first or second month.
translations.idiomatic: That winter snow gave way to unseasonable warmth and budding trees.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年三年正月丁已朔，上以疾不受朝賀。

translations.literal: Changqing 3 — In the first month of Changqing 3, dingsi new moon — because of illness the Emperor did not receive New Year congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing 3 opened with illness canceling New Year audience.

sentences.zh: 是日大風，昏翳竟日。

translations.literal: That day, great wind; gloom covered the day.
translations.idiomatic: That day wind and gloom shrouded the sky.

sentences.zh: 嗣郢王佐宜於崖州安置，坐妄傳禁中語也。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent of E Wang Zuo was to be settled at Yazhou for falsely spreading forbidden-palace words.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zuo was exiled to Yazhou for palace gossip.

sentences.zh: 敕不得買新羅人為奴婢，已在中國者即放歸其國。

translations.literal: An edict forbade buying new Silla people as slave servants; those already in China were to be sent back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Buying Silla slaves was forbidden and existing slaves freed.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎王起奏：當司所試貢舉人，試訖申送中書，候覆訖下當司，然後大字放榜。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Qi memorialized: when his office tested tribute candidates and testing was finished they were sent to the Secretariat; after review was finished they were returned to his office — then large-character posting of the list.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi reformed the examination posting procedure.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 二月，天平軍監軍奏：節度使烏重胤病，牙將王贄割股肉以療，河陽節度使陳楚奏：移使府於三城，未有門戟，欲移懷州門戟于河陽。

translations.literal: Second month — Tianping supervising commissioner memorialized: military commissioner Wu Chongyin was ill; guard officer Wang Zan cut flesh from his thigh to treat him. Heyang military commissioner Chen Chu memorialized: moving the commissioner office to Three Cities, there were no gate halberds — he wished to move Huai prefecture gate halberds to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Second month brought memorials on Wu Chongyin's illness and Heyang ritual arms.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both were approved.

sentences.zh: 廣東省議大夫殷侑奏禮部貢舉請置《三傳》、《三史》科，從之。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Doctor Yin You memorialized asking the Ministry of Rites examination to establish Three Traditions and Three Histories subjects — approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yin You added Three Traditions and Three Histories to the examinations.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At Revenue,

sentences.zh: 崔倰卒。

translations.literal: Cui Cong died.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Cong, the revenue minister, died.

sentences.zh: 三月丁已，宰臣百僚賜宴於曲江亭。

translations.literal: Third month, dingsi — chief ministers and the hundred officials were granted feast at Qujiang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the court feasted at Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 敕應禦服及器用在淮南、兩浙、宣歙等道合供進者，並端午誕節常例進獻者，一切權停。

translations.literal: An edict: imperial mourning dress and vessels due from Huainan, two Zhe, Xuanshe, and other circuits, and regular Dragon Boat and birthday tributes — all were temporarily stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute of mourning goods and festival gifts was suspended.

sentences.zh: 其鷹犬之類，除備蒐狩外，並令解放。

translations.literal: Hawks, dogs, and the like — except for hunting reserve — were all ordered released.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting birds and dogs were released except for the hunt.

sentences.zh: 以牛僧孺同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Niu Sengru was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru joined the council.

sentences.zh: 日晡晚後，有賊入通化門，鬥死者一人，傷者六人。

translations.literal: In the late afternoon, bandits entered Tonghua Gate; one died in fighting, six were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Late that day bandits fought at Tonghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 賜宣徽院從奉官錢一百二十貫文已下有差。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Office followers were granted one hundred twenty strings and below in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants received cash grants.

sentences.zh: 五月，山南西道奏移成州于寶井堡。

translations.literal: Fifth month — Shannan West memorialized moving Chen prefecture to Baojing Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan West moved Chen prefecture to Baojing.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使牛元翼卒。

translations.literal: Shannan East military commissioner Niu Yuanyi died.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yuanyi died.

sentences.zh: 秘書少監李隨奏請造當司圖書印一面，從之。

translations.literal: Secretariat Vice Supervisor Li Sui memorialized requesting one History Office book seal — approved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sui received a History Office seal.

sentences.zh: 六月，宰相監修圖史杜元穎奏：史官沈傳師除鎮湖南，其本分修史，便令將赴本任修撰。

translations.literal: Sixth month — supervising compiler of maps and histories Du Yuanying memorialized: History Officer Shen Chuanshi, having been made Hunan military commissioner, should take his duty of compiling history and proceed to his post to compile.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanying ordered Shen Chuanshi to compile history in his new post.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 敕京兆尹、御史大夫韓愈宜放台參，後不得為例。

translations.literal: An edict: Jingzhao intendant and Censor-in-Chief Han Yu should be released from Secretariat audience duty — afterward this must not become precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu was excused from Secretariat audience, not as precedent.

sentences.zh: 七月，國子祭酒韋乾慶卒。

translations.literal: Seventh month — National University Chancellor Wei Qianqing died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wei Qianqing died.

sentences.zh: 八月，鄭、滑節度使曹華卒。

translations.literal: Eighth month — Zheng-Hua military commissioner Cao Hua died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Cao Hua died.

sentences.zh: 檢校尚書右僕射、戶部尚書馬總卒。

translations.literal: Acting Right Vice Director and Minister of Revenue Ma Zong died.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zong died.

sentences.zh: 興元節度使韋綬卒。

translations.literal: Xingyuan military commissioner Wei Shou died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou died.

sentences.zh: 上由復道幸興慶宮，至通化門，賜持盂僧絹二百匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor by the covered way went to Xingqing Palace; reaching Tonghua Gate he bestowed two hundred bolts of silk on the alms-bowl monk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Xingqing and gifted a monk at Tonghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 因幸五方，賜從官金銀鋌有差。

translations.literal: He then visited the Five Directions and bestowed gold and silver ingots to followers in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He then toured the Five Directions and rewarded followers.

sentences.zh: 九月，澤潞節度使劉悟進位平章事。

translations.literal: Ninth month — Zelu military commissioner Liu Wu was promoted to Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Wu entered the council.

sentences.zh: 賜宰臣百僚重九宴於曲江亭。

translations.literal: Chief ministers and the hundred officials were granted Double Ninth feast at Qujiang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The court held the Double Ninth feast at Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 南詔王丘佺進金碧文絲十有六品。

translations.literal: Nanzhao King Qiu Xian presented sixteen kinds of gold, jade, brocade, and patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao sent sixteen kinds of treasure and silk.

sentences.zh: 十月，以京兆尹韓愈為兵部侍郎，以御史中丞李紳為江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Tenth month — Jingzhao intendant Han Yu was made Vice Minister of War; Censor-in-Chief Li Shen was made Jiangxi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Han Yu took War and Li Shen went to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉與李紳不協，紳有時望，恐用為相。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Fengji was at odds with Li Shen; Shen had contemporary reputation — Fengji feared he would be used as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji feared Li Shen's reputation would bring him to the council.

sentences.zh: 及紳為中丞，乃除韓愈為京兆尹、兼御史大夫，仍放台參。

translations.literal: When Shen became censor-in-chief, Han Yu was then made Jingzhao intendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, still released from Secretariat audience.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji named Han Yu Jingzhao intendant to block Shen.

sentences.zh: 紳性峭直，屢上疏論其事，遂與愈辭理往復，逢吉乃兩罷之。

translations.literal: Shen's nature was stern and upright; he repeatedly submitted memorials debating the matter — thus he and Yu argued back and forth, and Fengji then dismissed both.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen's protests led Fengji to remove both men.

sentences.zh: 然紳出而愈留。

translations.literal: Yet Shen went out while Yu remained.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen left the capital while Han Yu stayed.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜元穎罷知政事，除成都尹、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Du Yuanying ceased governing affairs and was made Chengdu intendant and Jiannan West military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanying left the council for Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 龍武統軍陳楚卒。

translations.literal: Dragon Martial commander-in-chief Chen Chu died.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chu died.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎韓愈為吏部侍郎，新除江西觀察使李紳為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Han Yu was made Vice Minister of Personnel; newly appointed Jiangxi observation commissioner Li Shen was made Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu took Personnel and Li Shen Revenue.

sentences.zh: 紳既罷除江西，上令中使就第賜玉帶，紳因除敘泣而請留，中使具奏，故與愈俱改官。

translations.literal: Shen, having been removed from Jiangxi, was ordered by palace envoy to his residence to bestow jade belt; Shen, citing removal, wept and requested to remain — the palace envoy fully reported — hence together with Yu his office was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen wept and begged to stay; both men were reassigned.

sentences.zh: 召翰林學士龐嚴對，因賜金紫。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Pang Yan was summoned to answer; he was then granted gold-purple.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Yan was summoned and honored with gold-purple.

sentences.zh: 賜內園使公廨本錢一萬貫，軍器使三千貫。

translations.literal: Ten thousand strings capital were granted the Inner Gardens Office and three thousand to the Armory Office.
translations.idiomatic: Inner offices received capital grants.

sentences.zh: 杜元穎赴鎮蜀，上御安福門餞，因賜皇城留守及金吾衛率等帛有差。

translations.literal: Du Yuanying departed to govern Shu; the Emperor at Anfu Gate saw him off and bestowed silk in graded amounts to the Imperial City intendant and Golden Guard commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor farewelled Du Yuanying at Anfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 十一月，上御通化門，觀作毗沙門神，因賜絹五百匹。

translations.literal: Eleventh month — the Emperor went to Tonghua Gate to watch construction of the Vaisravana image and bestowed five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor watched the Vaisravana statue raised.

sentences.zh: 停浙東貢甜菜、海蚶。

translations.literal: Zhedong tribute of sweet vegetables and sea clams was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhedong's sweet vegetable and clam tribute ended.

sentences.zh: 十二月，浙西觀察使李德裕奏去管內淫祠一千一十五所。

translations.literal: Twelfth month — Zhexi observation commissioner Li Deyu memorialized removing 1,015 illicit shrines within his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu tore down 1,015 illicit shrines in Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年四年正月辛亥朔，上御殿受朝如常儀。

translations.literal: Changqing 4 — In the first month of Changqing 4, xinhai new moon — the Emperor attended the hall and received audience as normal ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing 4 opened with normal New Year audience.

sentences.zh: 上餌金石之藥，處士張皋上疏切諫，上悅，召之，求皋不獲。

translations.literal: The Emperor took metal-and-stone elixir medicine; Recluse Zhang Gao submitted a memorial sharply remonstrating — the Emperor was pleased and summoned him, but Gao could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: A recluse warned against elixirs; the emperor sought him in vain.

sentences.zh: 澤、潞判官賈直言新授諫議大夫，劉悟上表乞留，從之。

translations.literal: Zelu administrative aide Jia Zhiyan, newly appointed Remonstrating Doctor, Liu Wu submitted a memorial begging to retain him — approved.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu kept his aide Jia Zhiyan at court.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書致仕孔戣卒。

translations.literal: Retired Minister of Rites Kong Die died.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Die died in retirement.

sentences.zh: 辛未，上大漸，詔皇太子監國。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Emperor grew gravely ill; an edict ordered the crown prince to supervise the state.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Muzong ordered the crown prince to rule in his stead.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上崩於寢殿，時年三十。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Emperor died in the bedchamber — he was thirty years old.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Muzong died at thirty.

sentences.zh: 群臣上諡曰睿聖文惠孝皇帝，廟號穆宗。

translations.literal: The hundred officials submitted posthumous title Sagacious, Cultured, Gracious, Filial Emperor; temple name Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Sagacious Cultured Gracious Filial Emperor, temple name Muzong.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚申，葬於光陵。

translations.literal: On gengshen of the eleventh month he was buried at Guang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Guang Mausoleum in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：臣觀五運之推遷，百王之隆替，亦無常治，亦無常亂，在人而已，匪降自天。

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】 The history officer says: Your servant observes the five phases' shifting and the hundred kings' rise and fall — there is no constant order, no constant chaos; it lies in men, not sent down from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal opens: order and chaos depend on men, not Heaven.

sentences.zh: 當軒黃禦宇之秋，則百年無事；

translations.literal: In the years when the Yellow Emperor held the realm, a hundred years passed without incident;
translations.idiomatic: Under a sage founder, centuries could pass in peace;

sentences.zh: 及商辛握圖之日，則四海橫流。

translations.literal: when Shang Xin grasped the map, the four seas flowed in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: under a tyrant the realm drowned in chaos.

sentences.zh: 昔章武皇帝國命之不行，惜朝綱之將墜，乃求賢俊，總攬英雄，果能扼大盜之喉，制奸臣之命。

translations.literal: Formerly when Emperor Zhangwu saw the state's commands not obeyed and grieved that court discipline was about to fall, he then sought worthy men and gathered heroes — and truly was able to seize the great robber's throat and control treacherous ministers' lives.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, seeing discipline fail, gathered heroes and throttled rebellion.

sentences.zh: 五十載已終之土，復入提封；

translations.literal: Fifty years of ended soil returned within the tribute borders;
translations.idiomatic: Fifty years of lost territory returned to the map;

sentences.zh: 百萬戶受弊之氓，重蘇景化。

translations.literal: a million households of suffering commoners revived under enlightened transformation.
translations.idiomatic: millions of the afflicted breathed again under his rule.

sentences.zh: 元和之政，幾致升平。

translations.literal: Yuanhe government nearly reached full peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe rule nearly reached peace.

sentences.zh: 鴟梟方革於好音，龍鼎俄傷於短祚。

translations.literal: The owl and kite had just changed to good music when the dragon cauldron was soon wounded by brief fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Just as harmony returned, brief reign shattered it.

sentences.zh: 苟或時有平、勃之佐，繼以文、景之才，則延湊、克融，自縮螳螂之臂；

translations.literal: If at the time there had been Ping and Bo as assistants, followed by Wen and Jing's talents, then Tingcou and Kerong would themselves have drawn in the mantis's arms;
translations.idiomatic: With worthy successors like Wen and Jing, Wang Tingcou and Zhu Kerong would have shrunk back;

sentences.zh: 智興、李祐，敢萌狗鼠之謀？

translations.literal: would Zhixing and Li You have dared sprout dog-and-rat plots?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing and Li You would never have dared mutiny.

sentences.zh: 強盜甯窺孟賁之金，餓隸不拾嬰兒之餌。

translations.literal: Strong robbers would not have eyed Meng Ben's gold; starving servants would not have picked an infant's bait.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels would not have looted the treasury; the desperate would not have stolen even crumbs.

sentences.zh: 觀夫孱主，可謂痛心，不知創業之艱難，不恤黎元之疾苦。

translations.literal: Observing this feeble lord, one may say it pains the heart — he did not know founding's hardship, did not pity the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: This weak sovereign broke the heart: he forgot founding's cost and ignored the people's pain.

sentences.zh: 謂威權在手，可以力制萬方；

translations.literal: He thought authority in hand could by force control the ten thousand directions;
translations.idiomatic: He thought power in his fist could command the realm;

sentences.zh: 謂旒冕在躬，可以坐馳九有。

translations.literal: he thought the imperial cap on his person could by sitting drive the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: he thought the crown on his brow could rule while seated.

sentences.zh: 曾不知聚則萬乘，散則獨夫，朝作股肱，暮為仇敵。

translations.literal: He never knew gathered is ten thousand chariots, scattered is a lone man — morning as arms and legs, evening as enemies.
translations.idiomatic: He never saw that unity makes an empire and division makes a lone man, ministers become enemies overnight.

sentences.zh: 仲長子所謂「至於運徙勢去，獨不覺悟者，豈非富貴生不仁，沉溺致愚疾。

translations.literal: What Zhongchangzi called "when fortune shifts and power departs, alone without awakening — is it not that wealth and rank breed inhumanity, indulgence breeds foolish sickness?
translations.idiomatic: As Zhongchangzi wrote, when fortune turns the indulgent ruler never awakens:

sentences.zh: 存亡以之迭代，治亂從此周復。

translations.literal: Survival and destruction iterate by it; order and chaos cycle through it.
translations.idiomatic: wealth breeds cruelty and indulgence breeds folly;

sentences.zh: 」誠哉是言也！

translations.literal: Thus the appraisal concluded: "Truly this saying!"
translations.idiomatic: So ends the appraisal: "How true that saying is!"

sentences.zh: 贊曰：惠王不令，敗度亂政。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: The gracious king was not virtuous; he destroyed measure and overturned government.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Muzong lacked virtue and wrecked the laws.

sentences.zh: 驕僻偶全，實賴遺慶。

translations.literal: Arrogance and perversity by chance intact — truly relying on leftover blessing.
translations.idiomatic: His reign survived only by his father's legacy.

sentences.zh: 皇皇上帝，為民立正。

translations.literal: Solemn High God, for the people establishing rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sets right for the people —

sentences.zh: 此何人哉，遽主鼎命。

translations.literal: What sort of man is this, to hastily master the cauldron mandate?
translations.idiomatic: what man was this to seize the throne so rashly?
